chunks: That was narrated by Sa'd ibn Abd Allah from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Malik from Zurara, all from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Mut'ah, by God, is the best; with it the Quran was revealed, and with it the Sunnah proceeded.
And from him (Abu Abdillah) from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn Isa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Which type of Hajj is best?' He said, 'Al-Mut'ah.' And how could anything be better than it, while the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) says: 'If I could reverse my matter from what I have concluded, I would do as the people did.'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: Al-Mut'ah (a type of Hajj or temporary marriage, contextually Hajj here)

ai.seo_question: What is the best type of Hajj according to Shia hadith and what is the evidence for its superiority?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar highlights the superiority of Al-Mut'ah (specifically Hajj al-Mut'ah or Qiran) as the best form of pilgrimage, with the Imam asserting that the Quran was revealed regarding it and the Sunnah proceeded with it. Citing the Prophet's statement that he would have performed it as the people did if he could reverse his decision, the narration underscores its foundational status in Shia jurisprudence. The reference to 'the people' often alludes to the majority practice during the Prophet's time, reinforcing the legitimacy of this mode of Hajj.
